articles.summary: STORY: :: Recorded on July 31:: Lisa Bernhard, Reuters:: Dean Smith, Portfolio Manager, FolioBeyondShares of Apple tumbled as much as 10% on Friday after a disappointing forecast showed that the iPhone maker was struggling to secure enough components as the AI-driven data center boom strains global supply chains.The drop, if sustained, would erase nearly $500 billion from Apple's market capitalization and return the crown of the world's most valuable company to AI chip giant Nvidia, days after reclaiming it.Meanwhile, shares of Amazon soared as much as 15% after the tech giant's solid cloud sales growth reinforced investor confidence in its massive AI bets."There's two really different trends going on," said Smith. "One is the hardware constraint, the [other is] cloud compute capacity, and those are going to continue to drive what we see in the AI investment thesis."Next week, the focus will remain on AI when SpaceX delivers its first quarterly earnings results since going public."There's no mystery about how many rockets they're firing off, we can see them," said Dean with a laugh. "So what I'm looking for in SpaceX is to see what is their plan for the AI side of the business."

articles.headline: Apple slides as supply snags cloud outlook, putting iPhone demand in focus
articles.summary: Apple shares dropped 7.3% before the bell on Friday as the tech giant warned that supply ‌constraints would hurt growth, prompting investors to look beyond near-term shortages to ‌gauge the hit from an expected iPhone price hike. The decline puts Apple on track to shed ​roughly $361.6 billion in market value, if the losses hold. The company's outlook highlighted a broader industry challenge, with AI-driven demand tightening supplies of advanced chips and memory, driving up costs and prolonging supply-chain bottlenecks across the technology sector.
